# Server selection versus connection and operation deadlines — concept pack

## Vocabulary

Terms this pack was harvested with, grouped by their relation to the concept; counts are units matched / sources. Zero-hit terms are listed under Coverage. On every unit line, `keywords:` names the terms that matched.

- **self**: Server selection versus connection and operation deadlines (18/3)

## Definitions

- [statement] The specification makes unset `timeoutMS` preserve existing timeout behavior. An explicit `0` means infinite operation time, but client limits such as `serverSelectionTimeoutMS` still apply. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/client-side-operations-timeout/client-side-operations-timeout.md · keywords: Server selection versus connection and operation deadlines
- [statement] CSOT is a best-effort maximum. It must cover all blocking sections, but drivers must document exceptions; the specification gives OCSP verification outside driver timeout control as an example that can exceed `timeoutMS`. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/client-side-operations-timeout/client-side-operations-timeout.md · keywords: Server selection versus connection and operation deadlines

## How it works

- [statement] Under CSOT, new TCP establishment uses `min(connectTimeoutMS, remaining computedServerSelectionTimeout)`; connection-handshake commands use the remaining `computedServerSelectionTimeout` as their `timeoutMS` value. These minima use the specification’s convention: when 0 means infinite, min(0, other) evaluates to other. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/client-side-operations-timeout/client-side-operations-timeout.md · keywords: Server selection versus connection and operation deadlines
- [statement] The PyMongo 4.11.2 timeout guide distinguishes `pymongo.errors.ServerSelectionTimeoutError` when no available server is found from `pymongo.errors.NetworkTimeout` when connection establishment or a server response misses the timeout. Its server-side `pymongo.errors.ExecutionTimeout` example warns that an operation may have partially completed. (low confidence) — https://pymongo.readthedocs.io/en/4.11.2/examples/timeouts.html · keywords: Server selection versus connection and operation deadlines
- [statement] When checkout requires a new connection under CSOT, TCP establishment uses `min(connectTimeoutMS, remaining computedServerSelectionTimeout)`. Network requests needed to create or authenticate the connection use the lesser of their specified default timeout and the remaining computed selection budget; without a specified default, they use the remaining budget. Handshake commands use the remaining computed selection budget as their `timeoutMS`. These minima use the specification’s convention: when 0 means infinite, min(0, other) evaluates to other. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/client-side-operations-timeout/client-side-operations-timeout.md · keywords: Server selection versus connection and operation deadlines

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] When `timeoutMS` is set, the CSOT specification requires ignoring deprecated timeout options, including `socketTimeoutMS` and `waitQueueTimeoutMS`; it preserves `serverSelectionTimeoutMS` and `connectTimeoutMS`. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/client-side-operations-timeout/client-side-operations-timeout.md · keywords: Server selection versus connection and operation deadlines
- [statement] The Node driver documentation defines `connectTimeoutMS` around establishment of a single TCP socket. The CSOT specification retains this limit and also uses it to derive a socket timeout for monitoring connections, which are outside `timeoutMS`. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options.md · keywords: Server selection versus connection and operation deadlines · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/client-side-operations-timeout/client-side-operations-timeout.md
- [statement] The CSOT specification requires drivers to ignore deprecated timeout settings when an operation sets or inherits `timeoutMS`; its deprecated configuration settings include `socketTimeoutMS`, `waitQueueTimeoutMS` and `wTimeoutMS`. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/client-side-operations-timeout/client-side-operations-timeout.md · keywords: Server selection versus connection and operation deadlines
- [statement] In the PyMongo 4.11.2 guide, `timeout()` bounds all operations inside its block under one deadline, whereas client `timeoutMS` applies to each API call. Nested `timeout()` blocks can shorten the outer deadline but cannot extend it; leaving the block restores the previous deadline. (low confidence) — https://pymongo.readthedocs.io/en/4.11.2/examples/timeouts.html · keywords: Server selection versus connection and operation deadlines

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] With `timeoutMS` set, the CSOT specification requires `min(serverSelectionTimeoutMS, remaining timeoutMS)` for selection and checkout. Checkout uses the remaining computed selection budget after selection, rather than receiving a fresh allowance. These minima use the specification’s convention: when 0 means infinite, min(0, other) evaluates to other. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/client-side-operations-timeout/client-side-operations-timeout.md · keywords: Server selection versus connection and operation deadlines · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/server-selection/server-selection.md
- [statement] Under CSOT, after constructing a wire message the driver checks the remaining budget before sending; it sets socket write and then read timeouts from the remaining `timeoutMS`. The response-read timeout covers the aggregate of all reads, rather than restarting for each read. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/client-side-operations-timeout/client-side-operations-timeout.md · keywords: Server selection versus connection and operation deadlines

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The Node.js driver documentation distinguishes `connectTimeoutMS` for one TCP connection, `serverSelectionTimeoutMS` for the allowed connection-selection period of `MongoClient.connect`, `socketTimeoutMS` for an already-connected socket, and `maxTimeMS` for execution after an operation reaches the server. The guide permits `maxTimeMS` only on individual operations or cursors. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options.md · keywords: Server selection versus connection and operation deadlines
- [statement] The CSOT specification defines `timeoutMS` as a best-effort operation budget covering server selection, connection checkout and server-side execution; PyMongo documents the same operation-wide scope. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/client-side-operations-timeout/client-side-operations-timeout.md · keywords: Server selection versus connection and operation deadlines · also: https://pymongo.readthedocs.io/en/4.11.2/examples/timeouts.html
- [statement] The server-selection specification warns that single-threaded blocking topology checks can exceed the selection timeout. CDRIVER-3451 describes a connection attempt whose `connectTimeoutMS` can outlast `serverSelectionTimeoutMS`; this is a documented boundary, not evidence about every released driver. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/server-selection/server-selection.md · keywords: Server selection versus connection and operation deadlines · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/CDRIVER-3451
- [statement] Mongoose documents `serverSelectionTimeoutMS` as applying both to initial `mongoose.connect()` attempts and to selecting a server for subsequent operations. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/Automattic/mongoose/blob/master/docs/connections.md · keywords: Server selection versus connection and operation deadlines · also: https://mongoosejs.com/docs/6.x/docs/connections.html
- [statement] The CSOT specification excludes commands executed by server-monitoring and RTT-calculation threads from `timeoutMS`. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/client-side-operations-timeout/client-side-operations-timeout.md · keywords: Server selection versus connection and operation deadlines
- [statement] If `timeoutMS` is unset and `waitQueueTimeoutMS` support remains, the specification preserves separate limits: `serverSelectionTimeoutMS` for selection, `waitQueueTimeoutMS` for checkout, `connectTimeoutMS` for socket establishment, and `socketTimeoutMS` for handshake commands. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/client-side-operations-timeout/client-side-operations-timeout.md · keywords: Server selection versus connection and operation deadlines
- [statement] The server-selection specification separately warns that single-threaded selection is not a hard deadline: a blocking immediate check can make selection take the configured timeout plus a blocking scan. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/server-selection/server-selection.md · keywords: Server selection versus connection and operation deadlines
